title: Tenant-aware rate shaping and capacity planning for embeddings endpoint
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and avoid noisy-neighbor effects on the embeddings endpoint by introducing tenant-aware rate shaping, prioritized admission control, and an improved capacity planning model for GPU pools. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and initial rollout of tenant-level shaping + predictive capacity estimator and includes observability and billing integrations.

Problem statement: High-volume tenants intermittently flood the embedding queue with slightly larger-than-usual batched requests, which causes queue buildup on shared inference pools. Current autoscaler reacts to queue depth and GPU utilization but is too slow to protect higher-tier customers, leading to increased p99 queue wait and emergency throttles. We need a solution that: (1) enforces per-tenant steady-state budgets, (2) prioritizes requests from reserved/enterprise customers, (3) improves the autoscaler's responsiveness through short-term forecasting, and (4) surfaces capacity and billing signals to PM and SRE teams.

Scope and non-goals: Includes implementation of per-tenant token budgets, leaky-bucket token bucket shaping at the front-door, priority classes (reserved, paid, best-effort), admission controller changes, a short-term forecast module for autoscaler, and dashboarding. Out of scope: full billing reconciliation (only hooks), long-term cost modeling beyond 90 days, and rewriting the serving runtime internals beyond necessary metrics and quotas hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant token shaping enforced at API gateway: configured token rates applied and validated in staging
Priority classes implemented: reserved, paid, best-effort with documented behavior and telemetry
Autoscaler uses 15-minute short-term forecast to provision burst capacity and reduces reactive scale-ups by >30% in synthetic burst tests
99th percentile queue wait for reserved tenants remains <200ms under mixed workload synthetic test (90th percentile tenant load spike)
Dashboards created: per-tenant queue depth, per-tenant tokens/sec, per-priority dropped requests; alerting thresholds added
Integration points created for billing (event hook) and Console feature flag to toggle tenant shaping per workspace

implementation_notes:
Design decisions: use leaky-bucket token-billing at gateway so we can shape before requests reach the serving fleet. Priority classes implemented with a two-queue admission controller: fast-path queue for reserved/paid and slow-path for best-effort. The autoscaler will be augmented with a short-term exponential smoothing forecast (alpha tuned per-queue) that estimates tokens/sec and expected queue growth; the autoscaler triggers ramp-up if forecasted GPU token demand exceeds capacity by configurable headroom.

Metrics to add: tenant.tokens_per_sec, tenant.queue_depth, tenant.dropped_requests, priority.wait_ms_p95, autoscaler.forecast_tokens_sec, autoscaler.scale_action_reason.

Testing plan: synthetic load harness that replays real tenant traces, benchmark scripts to validate p50/p95/p99 queue wait, chaos tests (kill GPU, network partition), cost simulation for forecast window tuning.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout by workspace: start with non-critical customers in staging, then 10% of production traffic (best-effort only), then enable reserved-priority handling for enterprise accounts. Monitor error budgets and rollback on SLO regressions.
